items.title: Ep52. How deep can plant roots grow?
items.desc: What’s happening beneath our feet? Lily and Max dig into how roots find water, why some stay near the surface while others grow astonishingly deep, and how roots help plants survive. Then they explore why a picked flower may keep opening for a little while, but can’t keep growing like a plant still connected to its roots. Join them for an underground adventure with a sleepy mole and a very ticklish nose!

items.title: Ep51. How long is the Great Wall of China?
items.desc: How long is the Great Wall of China? Is it really one continuous wall? Join Lily and Max as they explore its winding paths, watchtowers and fascinating history. Discover how different sections were built over many centuries, how guards sent messages across the landscape, and why the famous “visible from the Moon” claim isn’t true. A big question leads to an even bigger adventure!

items.title: Ep50. How did wolves turn into dogs?
items.desc: How did wolves become dogs? Lily and Max follow the clues back to the Ice Age, exploring how some wolves may have begun living near people and how natural selection gradually shaped their relationship. With ancient DNA, campfire scraps and a few very alert dogs, discover the long story behind one of our oldest animal friendships.

items.title: Ep49. Where does poo go when it’s flushed down the toilet?
items.desc: After discovering how toilets flush, Lily and Max follow the journey beyond the pipes. They explore how treatment plants remove rubbish, separate solids, and use helpful microorganisms to clean wastewater. Where does the treated water go and what happens to the solids? Find out in this curious, kid-friendly look at the hidden journey behind every flush.

items.title: Ep48. Why are trees important to our survival?
items.desc: Why are trees so important to our survival? Lily and Max explore the many jobs trees do: helping produce oxygen, storing carbon, providing food and shade, supporting the water cycle, protecting soil and creating homes for wildlife. Discover how trees connect to the air, water and living things we all depend on, and why caring for forests and woodlands matters.
